To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we demonstrate photon-pair emission in a microcavity filled with an optical nonlinear medium, which allows for the generation of correlated photon pairs with narrow bandwidths.

we demonstrate a liquid-filled microresonator for photon-pair generation, that the bandwidth of the emitted photon-pairs is $\sim 0.3$ GHz, that the emission wavelength can be tuned between 770 and $\sim 800$ nm, and that the pair correlation rate and the coincidence/accident ratio are increased by a factor of $10^3$.
we have realized a liquid-filled optical cavity and demonstrated photon-pair generation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of nonlinear microcavity devices based on liquid-filled microresonators.
the generation and manipulation of non-classical light in microcavity systems, with a focus on the development of a compact and efficient source of entangled photons.
the development of new methods for the generation and manipulation of quantum light in optical microcavities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a microcavity with a nonlinear medium completely filling the cavity leads to a significant improvement in the performance of the source.
the use of a microcavity filled with liquid as the nonlinear medium is a promising approach to generate correlated photon pairs for a wide variety of applications.
we have shown that liquid-filled microcavities can be used to generate entangled photon-pairs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated a new type of microcavity for nonlinear optics.
we have demonstrated the first photon-pair source based on a liquid-filled microresonator and have achieved a significant improvement in performance as compared to previous work.

we have demonstrated the generation of correlated photon pairs by spontaneous four-wave-mixing in a liquid-filled optical resonator and have shown that this approach can lead to an enhancement in the pair-correlation rate and a reduction in the accidental background.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of a liquid as a nonlinear optical medium and a microcavity as an optical resonator provides the best of both worlds.
a simple microcavity filled with a liquid is a promising platform for the generation of correlated photon-pairs.
liquid-filled optical microresonators provide an attractive platform for on-chip generation and manipulation of non-classical photon states.
